lines.ruling: Ruling: interface gap; i1040gi p. 98, Schedule 1, line 21 (the conditions for the deduction). The reply's two tests are the project's (a filing status other than married filing separately; no one on the return claimed as a dependent, person.sav_claimed) and it gives worksheet line 9 as the project does. It lacks the project's first alternative, $0 when no interest was paid (sli.interest zero), so it reads person.sav_claimed on returns with no student loan interest. The earlier rulings on this line found earlier replies to lack the dependent test; this reply has it. Re-reviewed because sli.interest was reworded (the older "(or your spouse if filing jointly)" in the eligible-student list is now the one spouse phrase; wording only, no expression changed). executable-triage-v2 (`.transcription/triage/2025/sli.json`, pass 970c08bc396c; 1,767 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 40 partial records): 1,759 of 2,307 comparisons agree; differences by kind {"candidate-refuses": 331, "candidate-unknown": 208, "project-unknown": 9}; on completed returns 101 candidate-unknown (on the six the record lists the project is $0 and the reply is unknown for person.sav_claimed); no value difference. The other differences are on refused or incomplete returns. No change to the data.

Ruling: representation; project retained. The worksheet gives no amount for married filing separately, which cannot take the deduction; the project enters zero there and the second enters $85,000. Neither reaches Schedule 1 line 21: sli.deduction is zero for married filing separately.
